subject: Real-time token pipeline lag — immediate mitigations and monitoring steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@finosa.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-01T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Real-time token pipeline lag — immediate mitigations and monitoring steps

Hi Alex,

Thanks for flagging the slow streaming behavior this morning — we saw the same symptom on our side between ~09:05–09:45 PDT: responses returned in 2–3 chunk bursts and a number of requests experienced >4s per-chunk delays.

What we know so far (initial):
- Impact: intermittent higher latency on streaming/chat endpoints for a subset of edge shards handling Finosa traffic; not a full outage but noticeable user experience degradation.
- Likely cause: an interaction between the token-pipeline scheduler and a kernel-selection fallback which briefly promoted some requests to a slower execution path under spike conditions.

Immediate mitigations we have applied (and recommended client changes):
1) Temporary routing: we pushed your traffic to a dedicated inference pool for the affected region (this reduces cross-tenant variance).
2) Lighter model variant: enabled the q2_KV-lite variant for sessions that requested streaming to reduce kernel fallback probability.
3) Short-term config for clients: if you can, set your streaming chunk_timeout to 6000ms and enable client-side incremental-ACK (if available). This reduces observed reordering and triggers faster client-side fallbacks. Example: stream_chunk_timeout=6000, max_stream_bytes=4096.
4) Server-side throttling: we tightened the per-session token window for a rolling 15m window to avoid spikes in the scheduler.

Attachments: a small bundle of kernel dumps from the affected nodes is attached (attachment: kernel_dumps.tar.gz, text). We sanitized tenant IDs.

Next steps:
- We're conducting a targeted runbook and a short patch for the scheduler today. Rishi and the infra team are on it.
- I'll follow up with a postmortem and a timeline for the permanent fix within 48 hours.

Can you confirm: which workspace IDs you saw the most impact on and whether you can accept the temporary lighter-quant variant for the next 24–48 hours?

Apologies for the disruption — we know latency like this degrades product trust and we're treating this as P1 for Finosa traffic until resolved.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Park <alex.park@finosa.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-01T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Real-time token pipeline lag — immediate mitigations and monitoring steps

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the quick response and the mitigations — we confirmed the same window on our side. Most of the customer complaints came from workspace IDs: finosa-prod-12, finosa-prod-14. Our support team logged roughly a 18% increase in perceived chat latency during that 40-minute window.

We approved the temporary lighter-quant variant for the short term. Two asks: one, can you send a summarized ETA for the permanent fix (we're preparing a customer status update), and two, we'd like to request an operational credit for the impact window — I'll open a ticket but wanted to mention it here so it's on your radar.

Attached are application-side logs matching the timestamps (we redacted user PII).

Appreciate the rapid handling.

—Alex
Alex Park
Head of Product — Conversational AI
Finosa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-01T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Real-time token pipeline lag — internal ops notes

Tessa / team,

Quick internal summary of what ops found while triaging:
- Root cause: an edge scheduler race that, during a sudden burst of short chats, caused some requests to be routed to a fallback kernel path with suboptimal memory layouts. This increases per-token latency for streaming chunks.
- Scope: ~12% of requests against 3 edge shards in us-west-2; correlation with a spiky inbound pattern from finosa-prod-12 and -14.
- Immediate actions completed at 09:30 PDT: forced-routing off the affected shards, applied conservative token-window limits, and enabled the q2_KV-lite runtime for Finosa sessions.

Planned follow-ups (ops plan):
1) Patch for scheduler race (low-risk, roll-forward) — patch ready, will roll to canary within 2 hours. (attachment: scheduler_patch.diff).
2) Add a telemetry alert for kernel-fallback rate > 1% sustained for 5m.
3) Postmortem + customer note draft (we should include an offer for credit and a scheduled sync).

I'll handle rollout and canary monitoring — Sean, please coordinate the telemetry dashboards and increase retention for the affected shard metrics for the next 7d. Marissa, will you own the customer communication cadence and the credit proposal?

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Inference Infrastructure

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@finosa.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-02T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary: streaming latency spike on 2028-10-01 (Finosa) — root cause and next steps

Hi Alex,

This is the follow-up postmortem and remediation plan for the streaming latency spike Finosa experienced on 2028-10-01. Thank you for the logs and for allowing the q2_KV-lite variant while we worked through fixes.

Executive summary:
- Incident window: 2028-10-01 09:05–09:45 PDT.
- Impact: intermittent increases in per-chunk streaming latency (average chunk latency increased from ~250ms to 1.4s for affected sessions).
- Root cause: a race condition in the token-pipeline scheduler that, under a burst of short-session requests, triggered a fallback to a slower kernel selection; this affected a small set of edge shards.

What we did:
- Immediate: routed Finosa traffic away from affected shards, enabled q2_KV-lite for your sessions, and tightened token-window controls.
- Fix: deployed a scheduler patch to remove the race condition (canary -> full roll by 2028-10-01 12:40 PDT).
- Monitoring: added an alert for kernel-fallback rate and extended metric retention for the affected shard series to 14 days.

Customer impact and remedy:
- We estimate the user-facing impact affected ~18% of your streaming requests during the 40-minute window.
- We're prepared to offer an operational credit for the impacted window — Marissa will follow up with a proposed credit amount and a short credit memo.

Ongoing actions for prevention:
1) Add regression tests to cover short-session burst patterns in the scheduler test harness.
2) Improve canary traffic shape to include synthetic short chats.
3) Quarterly review of kernel-selection telemetry and automated rollback triggers.

Attachments: postmortem-finosa-20281002.pdf (summary + telemetry graphs) and the scheduler patch (scheduler_patch.diff) if you'd like technical details.

If you're available, I'd like to schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through the postmortem and the credit memo. Please suggest a time and I will send a calendar invite.

Thanks again for your patience — we take these incidents seriously and will follow through on the remediation and credits.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Account Lead, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
